# PowerShell and C# API parity

I use the same domain names for cmdlet parameters, C# configuration and fluent calls. PowerShell keeps numeric duration parameters with units and default-off switches; C# keeps TimeSpan values and Boolean properties.

The contract covers **97 commands**, **1018 parameters** and **266 reachable public types**. The metadata gate checks names, types, sets, positions, defaults, nullability and member paths. Rendering and triplet tests check behavior.

Table and List remain named shortcuts to Show-Console’s shared view implementation. Read-* returns answers; New-ConsoleForm/Menu defines a question workflow; Show-ConsoleApp runs a persistent reactive application.

Typed Options on export, form, menu and replay operations expose the corresponding C# configuration. I can pass a PowerShell hashtable, for example `Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Html -Options @{ Width = 100; Padding = 8 }`. Options and individual settings are mutually exclusive; the supplied request is not modified.

## Individual member decisions

Native host hooks, runtime models and equivalent representations are listed individually. These decisions do not exempt a namespace or hide newly added options.

| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ShellPrompt.Path` | RuntimeOwned: PowerShell supplies its current provider location; a C# shell host supplies its own path. | Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Feature Prompt obtains this data from the owning PowerShell session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ShellPrompt.Succeeded` | RuntimeOwned: PowerShell supplies the last native/pipeline outcome; a C# shell host supplies its own command result. | Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Feature Prompt obtains this data from the owning PowerShell session. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Alignment` | EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock and RichText share alignment behavior; PowerShell exposes Alignment on its canonical RichText result. | Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Content` | EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock stores one string; PowerShell’s canonical text command returns RichText pieces usable in cells as well as block rendering. | Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.IsMarkup` | EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock selects parsing with a Boolean; PowerShell separates literal Text from explicit Markup input. | Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Overflow` | EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock and RichText share overflow behavior; PowerShell exposes Overflow on its canonical RichText result. | Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Role` | EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock stores a block role; PowerShell applies the same Role through RichText’s base style. | Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget. |
| `ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeHierarchyOptions.Identity` | CSharpOnly: A native graph identity delegate supports custom/AOT C# nodes; the PowerShell hierarchy adapter owns wrapped-object identity. | Use the canonical PSObject identity and bounded tree traversal. |
